name: tm_break_only

source.title: This Guy QUIT His Job for PROP TRADING. So I STOLE His Strategy

entry.words: CONTROL of tm_hurst_ac_break: the same 5-bar break, the same exits and trailing stop, with BOTH filters (Hurst, autocorrelation) switched off: what the two filters add.

taught: CONTROL, not taught: the video's rule without its two filters
not_run: The Hurst proxy formula is not given (it is in the seller's indicator); this sheet's is the uncentered variance ratio of 5-bar to 1-bar changes over 20 bars, x 100 (50 = random walk, a straight line = 100). It does not know the direction of the trend.
The autocorrelation is read on 1-bar close changes at lag 5 over 20 bars (the video glosses over the lag and the series).

The evening session 18:00-23:59 ET is NOT run: the engine refuses one window across midnight. The video's chart is 24 hours; this runs 00:00-15:58 ET only, one position at a time, flat 15:58 (house rule).
The indicators restart at 00:00 ET, so the first signal of a day is at 06:30 ET (26 fifteen-minute bars).
Position size by ATR (the firm's per-trade loss cap) is not run: 1 contract a cell; sizing is read afterwards.
His real exits and his scale-ins on pullbacks are discretionary and are not run.
The short side is not shown in the video and is not run.
The ATR is the simple mean of the last 20 true ranges (TradingView's ta.atr is Wilder's RMA: a small difference), frozen at the signal bar.

The control's random entries use the same 4 ATR stop and 5 ATR target as plain brackets WITHOUT the trailing stop (the lane's random entries have no trailing); the filter-off sheet (tm_break_only) is the like-for-like control.
No cap on trades a day is taught; max_trades 20 is the engine's bound for the one instance.
